name: Outlook Rules

evidence.rationale: Applying current Outlook patches reduces abuse of rule-triggered Visual Basic and related persistence mechanisms. It does not prevent all malicious mailbox-rule activity or activity performed through valid cloud-account access.

Applying current Outlook updates reduces abuse of rule-triggered execution mechanisms. This does not prevent all malicious mailbox-rule activity or activity performed through valid cloud-account access.

Vendor patches address Outlook mechanisms that adversaries may use to establish rule-triggered persistence or execution. Requiring current supported Outlook versions ensures the relevant security changes are applied.

Host-based intrusion prevention capabilities can enforce Attack Surface Reduction rules that prevent Office applications from creating child processes or writing potentially malicious executable content to disk.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
